title: hided WebSocket contract
description: Handshake, server frames, close reason codes, path refusal reason codes, and client dispatch events for hided.

serverFrame.description: snapshot/delta carry the core state; error answers a malformed client event; directory_list answers a `remote_file_list` for the `local` target or a `file_list`, and path_refused answers any event whose path failed its boundary - the $HOME line for `remote_file_list` and `create_workspace`, the checkout-root line for `file_list`, `file_open`, `reveal_path`, `file_save`, `file_create`, `dir_create`, `path_rename`, `path_move`, `path_trash` and `file_bytes` (see directoryList and pathRefused). file_bytes_error answers a `file_bytes` read the daemon could not serve as bytes (see fileBytes). directory_changed announces that a watched folder changed, so the client re-reads that one folder (see directoryChanged). attachment_refused answers an `attachment_stage` or `attachment_commit` that could not be staged (see attachments). file_index_result answers a `file_index` query with the ranked checkout paths (see fileIndex). A `file_bytes` read that succeeds is answered with one or more binary frames on the same socket, not a text frame (see fileBytes).

directoryChanged.description: Payload of a directory_changed frame: the watched folder whose contents changed. The daemon watches the focused checkout's root and its most recently expanded folders, at most 64 in total (the root counts); a change within 200 ms of the last one for the same folder is coalesced into the frame already sent. A client re-reads the one folder this names, which is the Explorer's live refresh without a reload.

pathRefusalReason.description: outside_home: the real path is not under $HOME (a symlink target counts). home_root: $HOME itself cannot be a workspace. outside_checkout: the path is not under any registered checkout root, which is the reason an explorer event gets for a path under $HOME that no checkout covers. not_found: nothing exists there. not_a_directory: a file where a directory was needed. not_a_file: a directory where a file's bytes were needed. invalid_path: empty, relative, contains `..` or NUL, or an item name that is empty, `.`, `..`, or holds a `/`.

directoryList.description: Payload of a directory_list frame. kind names the event that asked: a `remote_file_list` for the `local` target lists the visible subdirectories of root_path under $HOME, and a `file_list` lists the children of a folder under a registered checkout root - files and directories, hidden names included, `.git` and a symlink that leaves the root absent, directories first and then the natural name order the macOS Explorer uses. root_path is the real path that was listed (a request of `~` lists home and answers with its path). is_directory is what the Explorer draws and opens by; a `remote_file_list` answer carries directories only, so every entry in it is one. truncated is true past the listing cap.

pathRefused.description: Payload of a path_refused frame: the event kind that carried the path, the path as sent, and why hided did not forward it. A `file_create` or `dir_create` whose name failed the shape check, and a `path_rename` whose new name did, carry that name as the path.

attachments.description: The web cannot name a dropped file's path, so it uploads bytes for hided to stage, then commits them. `attachment_stage` {request_id, name, size, clipboard} opens one staged file (an over-cap size is refused at once); the bytes follow as binary frames, each framed like a file_bytes frame but client to server: a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON {request_id, offset, eof}, then that chunk's bytes. `attachment_commit` {request_id, pane_id, bracketed_paste, clipboard, stages} turns the staged files into the one `terminal_attachment` event the Swift shell sends, with the staged paths as its `paths`; a clipboard commit names no paths, because the image was staged at the path the core reads it from, and hided then reports `terminal_attachment_ready` itself. Caps: 20 MiB per file, 40 MiB and 8 files per batch. hided answers `attachment_refused` {request_id, reason} when a stage or commit fails or exceeds a cap; reason is one of invalid_request_id, too_large, batch_too_large, too_many_files, staging_full, stage_failed, forward_failed, no_pane, unknown_stage, stage_incomplete. Each stage id and name is flattened to one path component and refused otherwise; staged bytes are bounded at 256 MiB (a freshly committed file is spared for 60 s, and a full set of them refuses the new stage rather than unlinking one). The shell's own attachment events (terminal_attachment, terminal_attachment_ready, terminal_attachment_action) are the daemon's to send: a client that sends one is answered with an error frame and it never reaches the core. The core still owns the terminal side: its own refusal arrives in the snapshot's async operations.

attachmentRefused.description: Payload of an attachment_refused frame: the request that failed and why nothing was staged.

fileIndex.description: A client `file_index` event asks for the files of a registered checkout that match a query: {root, query}. The daemon walks the checkout once, honoring .gitignore (and .git/info/exclude and the global ignore file) without a git process, caps the index at 50,000 files, and answers with a file_index_result frame: {root_path, query, files: [{path, relative_path}], truncated, indexing}. `files` is ranked by the Swift fuzzy score, best first, at most 80; `path` is absolute so the client can open it, `relative_path` is what the palette shows. The first query for a root answers `indexing: true` while the walk runs; `truncated` marks a checkout whose index hit the cap. A root that is not a registered checkout is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_index.

fileIndexResult.description: Payload of a file_index_result frame: the root that was searched, the query, the ranked files, whether the index is truncated, and whether the walk is still running.

fileBytes.description: A client `file_bytes` event asks for a regular file's bytes under a registered checkout root: {request_id, path, offset, length}. `length` null or absent reads to the end of the file; `offset` defaults to 0. The daemon answers with one or more binary frames, each framed as a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON as UTF-8, then that chunk's bytes. The header is {type: "file_bytes", request_id, path, offset, total, eof}: offset is where this chunk starts in the file, total is the file's whole size, and eof marks the last frame. A read past MAX_FILE_BYTES (256 MiB) or a disk failure is answered with a file_bytes_error text frame instead: {request_id, path, reason} where reason is too_large or read_failed. A path that fails the boundary is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_bytes.

fileBytesError.description: Payload of a file_bytes_error frame: the read that failed and why.
